articles.title: The Biggest Security Myth I Believed as a Beginner
articles.excerpt: When I first started learning about computer security, I thought one thing mattered above everything else: Encryption. I believed that if I picked the strongest encryption algorithm, my software would…
articles.body: When I first started learning about computer security, I thought one thing mattered above everything else: Encryption. I believed that if I picked the strongest encryption algorithm, my software would automatically become secure. I couldn't have been more wrong. Security Isn't One Algorithm Today we have excellent cryptographic primitives. AES. ChaCha20. Fernet. PBKDF2. Argon2. They're all powerful when implemented correctly. But after spending months building a Windows desktop security application, I realised something: Most security failures don't happen because AES is weak. They happen because of poor engineering decisions. Weak password handling. Bad key management. No logging. Ignoring physical access. Blocking the UI while performing sensitive operations.

articles.title: AI will never replace tech workers because AI is not human
articles.excerpt: When we talk about AI these days, we're usually talking about large language models. To an LLM, the only reality it knows is data, and to be more specific, text data. Even when it looks at a photo, it…
articles.body: When we talk about AI these days, we're usually talking about large language models. To an LLM, the only reality it knows is data, and to be more specific, text data. Even when it looks at a photo, it's translating that photo into text data that it can understand through a vision encoder. But for humans, text is a small part of how we experience reality. Until the last few hundred years, text played almost no role in the average person's life. Most of human experience has been done through the senses or verbal communication, not through any sort of written text. Even if most modern humans do read, it is not the primary way that we experience our lives. This shows a fundamental difference between how humans and AI experience reality, and it doesn't stop there.

articles.title: Building AIAnalyzer: A Swift Static Analysis Tool That Knows When to Trust Its Own AI
articles.excerpt: I've spent 18 years shipping iOS apps — enterprise VoIP, automotive, retail — and one problem kept resurfacing regardless of the domain: codebases quietly rot, and Swift never had great tooling to cat…
articles.body: I've spent 18 years shipping iOS apps — enterprise VoIP, automotive, retail — and one problem kept resurfacing regardless of the domain: codebases quietly rot, and Swift never had great tooling to catch it early. Most static analysis tools are style linters, not architecture watchdogs. Nothing was really looking for God Objects, tangled responsibilities, or classes that had silently outgrown their purpose. So I built AIAnalyzer — a Swift CLI, distributed via Homebrew, that does two things: detects real architectural smells using SwiftSyntax, and offers AI-generated fix suggestions through a system that decides, in real time, whether to trust a fast local model or escalate to a stronger cloud one. The problem with "just use AI for everything" Bolting an LLM onto a dev tool is easy.

articles.title: A SpaceX rocket will crash into the moon next week, and scientists aren't sure what to expect
articles.excerpt: Scientists are preparing to study the effects of human-made impacts on the moon when a spent SpaceX rocket stage impacts the lunar surface on Aug. 5.
articles.body: On Aug. 5, Earth's moon is due for a human-made, high-speed impact from an identified flying object: a spent SpaceX Falcon 9 upper stage. The event will lead to a literal "dust up" on the lunar landscape. That Falcon 9 upper stage is a leftover from the launch that sent Firefly's Blue Ghost-1 lander to the moon on Jan. 15, 2025. Onboard the same flight was the Hakuto-R Mission 2 , called Resilience, a robotic lunar lander developed by the Japanese company ispace. And according to a new study by an international team published on the open-source arXiv server, the resulting impact plume may briefly be bright enough to see against the dark sky near the moon's edge. That means it might be visible to moongazers with sufficiently sensitive telescopes.

articles.title: This new app lets you root your Galaxy flagship without tripping Knox or unlocking the bootloader
articles.excerpt: The Root My Galaxy app uses a Linux kernel exploit to grant soft root access on older Snapdragon-based Galaxy flagships.
articles.body: Credit: Zac Kew-Denniss / Android Authority TL;DR A new open-source tool called “Root My Galaxy” uses a software exploit to grant temporary root access on select Samsung Galaxy flagships. The tool works without wiping data, unlocking the bootloader, or tripping Knox, preserving features like Secure Folder, Samsung Wallet, and Play Integrity. Root access is temporary and must be reapplied on every reboot, and devices running newer security patches or Exynos chipsets are currently excluded. Modding modern flagship phones has become an increasingly uphill battle. Samsung hasn’t been a stalwart in this space for a while, thanks to Knox, but the company went further and effectively killed bootloader unlocking on One UI 8 in several major regions.

articles.body: Studio Ghibli has weathered surprisingly few genuine critical disappointments across its four-decade history. It’s a studio best known for anime masterpieces, which is why calling a Studio Ghibli movie "bad" almost feels like a contradiction. While it does have a few “lesser” films in its catalog, from Earwig and the Witch to Ocean Waves (a sleeper hit if you ask me), no Ghibli film has been more persistently labeled the studio's weakest than Tales from Earthsea , which celebrates its 20th anniversary next month with a North American theatrical release.

articles.title: The action epic fantasy that Paramount tried it kill is a officially a global streaming smash hit
articles.excerpt: Mere days after its release, the new Avatar: The Last Airbender movie is a huge hit on Paramount Plus.
articles.body: The long-awaited follow-up to perhaps the single most beloved animated series of the late 2000s was supposed to be a huge theatrical event. Then in December, its wide release was canceled in favor of a straight-to-streaming release on Paramount Plus. A few months later, the entire movie leaked online following a server breach in April 2026. Fast-forward to today, mere days after its July 25 streaming release date, and it’s a massive hit on Paramount Plus as the platform’s number one movie both in the U.S. and worldwide.
